headline: High: Flowise’s default broad egress and filesystem access can leak or mis-handle shared chatflow data when paired with a non-runnable docs-only repo that offers no isolation controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible direct prompt-injection bridge is documented. Profile A is a non-runnable awesome-list with no I/O surfaces, while Profile B has files and browser/tool nodes but no shared channel to ingest A’s outputs by default. The pair lacks evidence of a direct communication path.
conditions: IF A is manually copied into a Flowise prompt or file input, injection becomes possible.
IF B is configured to ingest untrusted text from a shared workspace, prompt injection risk increases.
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces.
Disable automatic ingestion of external text into B flows.
Require manual review before copying content from A into B.
Use allowlisted prompt templates in B.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all imported content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: B reads and writes server filesystem data and sends configured tool/API traffic, while A is a docs-only repo with no runtime data classes. The pairwise leakage path is mainly through B handling chatflow inputs/outputs and uploaded files; A does not add a second data sink, so this is not high, but the default B surface is enough for sensitive data exposure in shared deployments.
conditions: IF B processes uploaded files containing secrets or PII, those contents can be exposed to configured model providers or tools.
IF A is used as a source of copied operational guidance, no direct data leak occurs from A itself.
mitigations: Restrict B to non-sensitive test data.
Disable file uploads in B flows that handle secrets.
Rotate any credentials already stored in B.
Separate chatflow workspaces by sensitivity.
requires-engineering: enforce per-flow data-loss-prevention checks.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or runtime capabilities, but B can write the filesystem and uses shared server datastore across instances. There is no evidence A can contend for the same mutable resources, so the conflict is one-sided rather than a true write-write collision. Uncertainty about deployment isolation pushes this above low.
conditions: IF B instances share the same writable directory, concurrent writes can collide.
IF the deployment maps A-derived artifacts into B’s server filesystem, B may overwrite them.
mitigations: Use separate directories per Flowise run.
Disable shared writable mounts.
Avoid placing A-derived artifacts in B’s workspace.
Serialize writes for concurrent B instances.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared datastore writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B can treat upstream inputs as flow nodes and act on them with tools, while A provides no runtime verification layer. Because A is not runnable and does not emit authoritative facts, the cascade is indirect, but B’s graph-based tool use means copied A content could be operationalized without validation.
conditions: IF A-derived text is pasted into a B flow as facts, B may act on it without verification.
IF B nodes are configured to send emails, API calls, or browser actions, downstream mistakes can propagate.
mitigations: Add a human review step before action nodes.
Mark A-derived inputs as untrusted in B.
Disable auto-execution for flows that consume external text.
Use validation nodes before any side-effecting tool.
requires-engineering: implement source-citation checks before actions.

E_compliance.rationale: A is a docs-only open-source repository with no touched data classes, so it does not itself create a residency or retention issue. B handles chatflow inputs/outputs and secrets, but the profiles do not show a specific jurisdiction mismatch or regulated data class. The compliance risk is therefore limited to documented gaps in B’s deployment, not the pair itself.
conditions: IF B is deployed with regulated data and a noncompliant retention policy, compliance risk increases.
IF B routes EU PII to non-EU services without a DPA, a higher severity applies.
mitigations: Review B retention settings.
Limit B to non-regulated data.
Document data flows for each chatflow.
Confirm provider DPAs before enabling sensitive flows.
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing controls.
